title: As US relations fray, Canada gets serious about its own launch industry
gist: US tariffs and '51st state' rhetoric pushed Canada to pursue sovereign launch, with Launch the North making initial C$8.33M awards to NordSpace, Reaction Dynamics and Canada Rocket Company. Canada Rocket Company is skipping small rockets for the 12.5-ton R-2 medium-lift vehicle targeting 2032, has raised $22.5M, is starting a Series A, and announced a $30M Jeremy Hansen engine test facility near London, Ontario.

insights.claim: Trump administration tariffs and talk of making Canada the 51st state have led the Canadian government to reassess reliance on the US across many areas, including sovereign access to space.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: US-allied friction is creating new state-funded demand for domestic defense and space industries among allies.

insights.claim: Canada's Launch the North program made initial awards of C$8.33 million to NordSpace, Reaction Dynamics and Canada Rocket Company for light-lift rockets, with larger awards signaled for the future.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Early government seed money identifies the likely national champions in Canadian launch.
insights.quote: The initial awards as part of Launch the North were modest, $8.33 million CAD

insights.claim: Canada's new Defense Industrial Strategy lists space as one of 10 priority capabilities, explicitly including space launch.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Defense budget framing gives Canadian launch a more durable funding base than civil space programs.
insights.quote: Space is one of the 10 capabilities outlined in the report, which includes “space launch” as a priority.
insights.locator: But sovereignty is back in vogue

insights.claim: Hugh Kolias predicts the Canadian government may eventually commit as much as half a billion dollars to sovereign launch capability, plus some guarantee of launch contracts.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: A ~C$500M program with anchor contracts would materially de-risk private Canadian launch ventures.

insights.claim: Kolias argues geopolitics has created an opportunity for Canadian industries broadly to build ambitious domestic capabilities as the country pulls back from globalism toward owning core economic and defense assets.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Deglobalization among US allies is a structural tailwind for domestic aerospace and defense suppliers.
insights.quote: I think the geopolitics has actually created a fantastic opportunity, not just for us, but for other Canadian industries to finally build real ambitious industries,

insights.claim: Since Canada canceled the Avro Arrow interceptor in 1959, its aerospace industry has largely languished and its satellites typically launch on American rockets.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Canada starts from a low base, so execution risk on sovereign launch is high.

insights.claim: Canada Rocket Company skipped the small-rocket phase after about 150 engineers, including SpaceX's director of Starship engineering, advised that building a smaller rocket does not de-risk a larger rocket program.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Challenges the small-launcher-first playbook, implying many light-lift startups may be stranded investments.
insights.quote: you’re not going to be able de-risk a rocket development program by building a smaller rocket

insights.claim: Kolias says roughly 90% of the technical and infrastructure work on a light-lift rocket gets thrown out when moving to a larger vehicle, making it almost a net new program.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Low technical carryover undercuts the value of small-launch experience as a path to medium lift.

insights.claim: The planned R-2 rocket resembles SpaceX's Falcon 9, with nine methane-fueled gas-generator engines, landing legs for future first-stage reuse, and up to 12.5 metric tons to low-Earth orbit, targeting launch readiness by 2032.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: A 2032 target means no near-term competition for incumbents but adds future medium-lift supply.
insights.quote: It could carry up to 12.5 metric tons to low-Earth orbit.
insights.locator: So the company set its sights higher

insights.claim: Canada Rocket Company has about 30 staff, many of them Canadian rocket scientists returning from SpaceX, Blue Origin and Rocket Lab, has raised $22.5 million and is launching a Series A.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Early-stage private investment opportunity in a sovereignty-backed launch play; talent repatriation is a signal.
insights.quote: the company has raised $22.5 million to date and is going to market with a Series A fundraise.

insights.claim: The company's $30 million Jeremy Hansen Test Facility on 50 acres leased from the Greater London International Airport Authority will host up to three stands able to test engines above 1 MN thrust, with E-1 engine testing starting in about two years.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Concrete infrastructure spend signals commitment, though engine testing remains roughly two years out.

insights.claim: Astronaut Jeremy Hansen's Artemis II flight, making him the first non-American in deep space, boosted Canadian space prestige even though it relied on the US program, which the author suggests could anchor future warm relations alongside independent Canadian launch.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Space patriotism supports political will for Canadian launch funding.
